scope: rc-1 PR feature/0.4.5 -> develop — diff-based security verdict for release v0.4.5 over git diff 68658783..5a8810ac (base = ship 0.4.4): 150 files, +16357/-1705. Surfaces reviewed: FR1 gate LAW predicate (features/spec_context/gate_policy.py, CWE-284), FR2 atomic write (core/atomic_write.py, CWE-59/377/732), FR6 write-time redaction seam (core/models/bugs.py, features/bugs/service.py, cli/commands/bugs.py, infrastructure/privacy_check.py), FR7 control-character sanitation (CWE-117), FR8 symlink refusal on specs init (CWE-59), certify detail capping (CWE-532), INV-6 + .dadaia/references sanction + core/workspace_layout.py, hooks/_common.py, public assets/persona/DADAIA.md diet, tests, specs/bugs/bugs.jsonl new events, and a gitleaks-style + operator-denylist scan of the delta. Dependency (CVE) and IaC lanes have no input in this delta — no manifest, lockfile, workflow, Dockerfile, compose or Terraform file changed.
verdict_reason: One HIGH blocking finding. The workspace's own range-scoped denylist chokepoint refuses this push: fed the real unpushed refspec (origin/feature/0.4.5 36e074e7 -> 5a8810ac, 104 commits), `dadaia ci push-gate-check` exits 1 with '13 object(s) carrying a denylisted term', layer 'foreign repo slug', masked term 'd…s' — a private consumer repo name committed into pushed material across 8 blobs of 6 paths, mostly under specs/releases/_ideas/0.5.0/** plus specs/releases/v0.4.5/reviews/RELEASE-VERDICT.md:131 and S3-qa-close.md:19. dd-gitflow-default §5 row 3 classifies that scan as Mechanical enforcement, so the rc-1 PR cannot be opened without `git push --no-verify`; the disclosure class is the operator's recorded second recurrence; and CI cannot detect it, because the foreign-slug layer derives from the local repos/ set which is empty on a runner — the pre-push hook is the only detector in the pipeline. Because the scan is object-scoped rather than tree-scoped, scrubbing the HEAD tree alone leaves 12 of 13 blobs reachable and still blocks; the offending commits in the unpushed range must be rewritten. Everything else in the delta is clean or positive: no secrets, no CVE/IaC input, public-privacy doctor green, 168 security-relevant tests green, and FR1/FR2/FR6/FR7/FR8 each verified to do what they claim (LAW predicate is zero-I/O and statically floored so a manifest edit cannot demote it; sanitation matches CPython's splitlines terminator set exactly with the A7.6 strip-then-mask ordering; atomic write cleans up on every failure path). Two non-blocking defects (MEDIUM: schema validation now runs on the pre-redaction object, so the persisted bug row is never validated; LOW: the same widening masks the context field in 5 of 7 consumer contexts) plus a LOW residual on the default `specs init` arm and a LOW standing note on atomic_write. Bug-surface axis: the delta REDUCES the bug surface of every feature it touches — FR2, FR6, FR1 and FR7 are each a collapse or a deletion, not an addition; the blocker is committed specs prose, not structure.

findings.message: 13 objects in the real push range carry a foreign private repo slug — the workspace's own pre-push denylist chokepoint BLOCKS this push (CWE-200).
findings.detail_md:
**Reproduce (exit code read directly, no pipe):**

```
printf 'refs/heads/feature/0.4.5 5a8810ac… refs/heads/feature/0.4.5 36e074e7…\n' \
  | .dadaia/.venv/bin/dadaia ci push-gate-check
```

`EXIT=1` — `[pre-push] BLOCKED: the pushed range publishes 13 object(s) carrying a denylisted term (DADAIA.md §7 — private names never enter public/pushed material)`, layer `foreign repo slug`, masked term `d…s` (13 chars). The term is a **consumer repo slug present under `repos/` in this workspace** — it is never echoed here or by the scanner (`denylist_scan.py:11-13`, CWE-532 masking).

**Range matters.** `origin/feature/0.4.5` is at `36e074e7`, local head at `5a8810ac` — 104 unpushed commits. The chokepoint is range-scoped over **every object**, not the tip tree, so the 13 offenders span 8 distinct blobs of 6 paths across 8 commits:

| blob | commit | path:line |
|---|---|---|

| `2b296266200c` | `bf033cf7` | `specs/releases/_ideas/0.5.0/TASKS.md:1183` |
| `cbd7a2e4380e` | `ae84021e` | `specs/releases/v0.4.5/reviews/RELEASE-VERDICT.md:131` |

At the HEAD tree the surviving hits are `_ideas/0.5.0/SPEC.md:1579`, `_ideas/0.5.0/TASKS.md:1183`, `_ideas/0.5.0/reviews/ai-engineer-definition-review.md:28`, `_ideas/0.5.0/reviews/bug-history-forensic-100.md:124` and `:243`, `v0.4.5/reviews/RELEASE-VERDICT.md:131`, `v0.4.5/reviews/S3-qa-close.md:19`, `:130`, `:172`.

`install_helpers.py:120`, `:485` and `bugs.jsonl:353,354,568,1008,1009` also match the slug but are **amnestied** by the v0.11.0 FR1 rule (same path, same value already in published prior text) — they are correctly NOT in the blocked set and require no action.

**Why this is HIGH, not cosmetic.** (a) `dd-gitflow-default` §5 row 3 classifies the range-scoped denylist scan as *Mechanical*, enforced by the pre-push hook — it is law, not advice, and it is currently RED for this exact refspec, so the rc-1 PR cannot be opened without `git push --no-verify`. (b) The disclosure class (a private consumer repo name in pushed material) is the operator's recorded **second recurrence**; a security APPROVE over a live, mechanically-detected third occurrence is precisely the failure this gate exists to prevent. (c) CI cannot catch it — the foreign-slug layer is derived from the local `repos/` set, which is empty on a runner, so the pre-push hook is the only detector in the whole pipeline.

**Note on scope discipline:** most offenders sit under `specs/releases/_ideas/0.5.0/**`, which the task brief explicitly says must never be staged. They are already committed on this branch.
findings.fix_recommendation: Scrub the foreign slug from the six paths above (replace with a generic placeholder such as 'a consumer repo' / '<consumer-slug>'), then rewrite the offending commits — the scan is object-scoped, so editing only the HEAD tree leaves 12 of 13 blobs reachable and still blocks. Use an interactive rebase or `git filter-repo --replace-text` over `36e074e7..HEAD` (the range is entirely unpushed, so no published history is rewritten), then re-run `dadaia ci push-gate-check` on the real refspec and require EXIT=0 before re-requesting a verdict. Separately consider whether `specs/releases/_ideas/0.5.0/**` belongs on this branch at all. Never use `--no-verify`.

findings.message: FR6 moved redaction after schema validation — the persisted bug row is never validated (CWE-20 data integrity).
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/cli/commands/bugs.py:245-265`: the CLI dropped its own `.redact()` call, builds `payload = model.to_dict()` from the **unredacted** model, validates that against `bug-event-v1.schema.json`, and only then calls `service.append_event(model)` — where `features/bugs/service.py:93` applies `event.redact(self._denylist_terms)`. **The object written to the append-only ledger is therefore never the object that was validated.**

This was harmless while `redact()` touched free text only. FR6 widened it: `core/models/bugs.py:357-360` now scrubs the whole `_OPTIONAL_STR_FIELDS` tuple (`core/models/bugs.py:204-221`), which includes the **structured** fields `severity`, `context`, `surface` and `component` — fields the pre-FR6 docstring deliberately excluded ('Structured/enumerated fields (severity, component, context, …) are not free text and are left untouched'). A denylist term that is a case-insensitive substring of a severity value would rewrite `severity` to `[REDACTED-TERM]` and land a row violating the schema's `enum: [LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL]`, undetected, in an append-only store that by law is never rewritten.

**Not exploitable in this workspace today** — verified against the live 18-term operator denylist: 0 terms collide with the severity enum, and `redact_text('HIGH', terms)` returns `HIGH` unchanged. The defect is the ordering, which makes correctness depend on operator-supplied data the code never constrains. The schema-mirror widening itself (A6.5) is the right call and closes the T-043-23 → T-044-62 hand-kept-list chain.
findings.fix_recommendation: Validate the object that is actually persisted: either redact before `to_dict()`/validate in `cli/commands/bugs.py`, or move schema validation inside `BugService.append_event` after `event.redact(...)`. One redaction pass, one validation pass, same object — do not reintroduce the double-redact AM-1 removed.

findings.message: FR6 masks the `context` field: 5 of 7 local context slugs redact to [REDACTED-TERM] in consumer bug ledgers.
findings.detail_md:
Concrete reachable consequence of the same `_OPTIONAL_STR_FIELDS` widening. Checked against the live denylist and the local `repos/` set: **5 of 7 context slugs** match a denylist term, so in those contexts every future `dadaia bugs append --context <slug>` persists `"context": "[REDACTED-TERM]"`. `dadaia-workspace` itself is unaffected (`redact_text('dadaia-workspace', terms)` returns it unchanged), so this repo's own ledger is clean and the 17 new `bugs.jsonl` events in this delta are correct.

Masking a private slug out of a committed ledger is arguably the intended privacy outcome — the issue is that it arrived as a **side effect** of 'mirror the whole optional-str tuple' rather than as a stated decision, and it silently drops routing metadata. No consumer of `BugEvent.context` exists in `features/bugs/service.py` today (the fold keys on `bug_id`), so nothing breaks now.
findings.fix_recommendation: Record an explicit ADR: either accept context masking as intended FR6 behaviour and note it in the feature memory atom, or exclude the enumerated/structured fields (`severity`, `context`, `surface`, `component`) from the denylist pass while keeping them in the IP/home-path pass — derived from the schema's own `enum`/structured markers, never a second hand-kept list.

findings.message: FR8 leaves the default `specs init` path outside the CWE-59 symlink refusal.
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/cli/commands/specs.py:329`:

```python
target = _resolve_specs_dir(specs_dir) if specs_dir else Path.cwd() / "specs"
```

Only the **explicit** `--specs-dir` arm reaches `core/specs_resolver.py:157`'s `path.is_symlink()` refusal. The `None` arm keeps the raw `Path.cwd() / "specs"`, and the guard immediately below it refuses only the Workspace-Root case (`Path.cwd() / ".dadaia").is_dir()`), never a symlink. So `cd repos/<slug> && dadaia specs init` with a planted `specs` symlink still scaffolds the whole template tree through it — the exact class T-044-40 closed for the explicit arm.

LOW: local only, requires an attacker-planted symlink plus the operator running `init` in that directory, and the impact is creation of fixed-name template files rather than disclosure. Related standing note: `is_symlink()` checks the final component only — a symlinked *parent* is still followed (pre-existing, unchanged by this diff).
findings.fix_recommendation: Apply the same refusal to the default arm — check `is_symlink()` on the computed `Path.cwd() / 'specs'` before scaffolding, reusing the resolver's existing refusal message rather than adding a second one (A8.2).

findings.message: core/atomic_write.py: no O_EXCL on the temp sibling, and preserve_mode defaults to False (CWE-377 / CWE-732).
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/core/atomic_write.py:60-75`. Two standing notes, neither a regression:

1. **No `O_EXCL`.** The temp sibling is created with `tmp.write_bytes()` / `tmp.write_text()`, which follow symlinks and do not fail on an existing path. The `uuid4().hex` name makes pre-creation infeasible, and the file is a **sibling of the destination** rather than in a world-writable temp directory, so the classic CWE-377 race does not apply. `os.replace` does not follow a symlinked **destination** — a symlinked target is replaced by a regular file rather than written through, which is the safe outcome.

2. **`preserve_mode=False` default.** A write over an existing restrictive-mode file widens it to the umask default. Verified non-regressive: all 11 replaced writers had exactly this behaviour (`presence.py`, `session_identity.py`, `hooks/_common.py` diffs show identical prior idioms); law files are re-chmod'd `0o444` at `infrastructure/install_helpers.py:170-173`; executable projections chmod `0o755` after write and `infrastructure/public_assets.py:1322-1335` reports a cleared exec bit as repairable drift. Cleanup-on-every-failure and the `contextlib.suppress` around it are correct — the `finally`/`replaced` flag covers the content-write and `os.replace` paths alike, closing the leaked-temp bug this consolidation supersedes.
findings.fix_recommendation: Optional hardening, not required for this PR: create the temp sibling with `os.open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY)`, and document in the docstring that a caller writing a mode-sensitive destination must pass `preserve_mode=True` (the four current callers that need it already do).

findings.message: Certify detail capping fixes a real CWE-532 blob leak; residual: only cwd is masked.
findings.detail_md:
`features/certification/service.py:84-125`. `_codex_probe_outcome` replaces the previous raw-blob echo (`RuntimeError(f"codex exec exited {rc}: {combined}")`) with a parsed `error.message`, the matching refusal line, or a byte-count marker, all routed through `_codex_capped_detail` — genuine improvement, `certify --json` no longer carries arbitrary subprocess output.

Residual, informational: the `Redactor` is seeded with `[str(cwd)]` only. An upstream 4xx `error.message` could still carry an account/org identifier; the 200-char cap bounds the blast radius but does not classify it. Acceptable — the field is an upstream auth-rejection message, not a token carrier.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action required for this PR. If the certify ledger is ever published, seed the Redactor with the operator denylist terms as well, reusing container.load_denylist_terms().

findings.message: FR7 control-character sanitation verified correct against Python's own splitlines terminator set (CWE-117).
findings.detail_md:
`core/models/bugs.py:249`:

```python
_UNSAFE_FORMAT_CHARS_RE = re.compile("[\\x00-\\x08\\x0b\\x0c\\x0e-\\x1f\\x7f\\x80-\\x9f\\u2028\\u2029]")
```

Cross-checked against CPython's `str.splitlines()` terminator set (`\n \r \v \f \x1c \x1d \x1e \x85 \u2028 \u2029`): every terminator except `\n`/`\r` is stripped — `\v`/`\f` explicitly, `\x1c-\x1e` inside `\x0e-\x1f`, `\x85` (NEL) inside the C1 range `\x80-\x9f`, plus `\u2028`/`\u2029`. TAB/LF/CR survive, and `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` escapes the entire C0 range including `\t\n\r`, so no field value can fragment a JSONL line that `JsonlBugStore.iter_events` splits on a literal `"\n"`. The C1 range is *not* escaped by `ensure_ascii=False`, which is exactly why stripping it is load-bearing. The A7.6 ordering (strip → IP → home → denylist, `core/models/bugs.py:263-271`) closes split-term evasion: a term interrupted by ESC or U+2028 re-joins into a contiguous substring before the masking passes run. Deleting rather than escaping is the right call for that reason.

**Live-ledger evidence:** the 17 new `specs/bugs/bugs.jsonl` events in this delta all parse as JSON and carry zero home-path, IPv4, e-mail or control-character hits.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action — the narrowing is correct and the read-side split is consistent with it.

findings.message: FR1 LAW predicate verified zero-I/O and statically floored; the repos/ loosening un-protects no projection (CWE-284).
findings.detail_md:
`features/spec_context/gate_policy.py:256-268` — `_is_law_path` is pure string splitting over two module-level frozensets bound once at import (`gate_policy.py:95-96` ← `core/workspace_layout.py:84-89`). `classify_path` (`gate_policy.py:279-302`) evaluates LAW **first**, before the `repos/` re-root, and performs no file I/O and no manifest read anywhere on the path — so editing `.dadaia/agentic/manifest.json` cannot demote a floored law path. That is the CWE-284 requirement, met.

The deliberate loosening (`repos/<slug>/AGENTS.md|CLAUDE.md`: LAW → MUTATING) un-protects no lib-originated projection: the live manifest carries **0 entries** under `repos/`, and `DADAIA_MD_HARNESS_TARGETS` projects the law only to the workspace root and the fixed harness dirs. Test coverage matches (`tests/unit/features/spec_context/test_gate_policy.py` — `test_manifest_tracked_law_projections_stay_law`, plus executed-path ALLOW assertions for the fresh and existing repo cases). 168 tests green across the security-relevant surfaces (`test_repo_self_scan`, `features/bugs/`, `core/test_atomic_write`, `spec_context/test_gate_policy`, `cli/test_cli_specs_init_symlink_refused`, `certification/test_service_codex_detail_redaction`), run with `-p no:cacheprovider`.

findings.message: No dependency, IaC or CI input in this delta; public-privacy doctor green; FR5 scan-vacuity guard is a net hardening.
findings.detail_md:
**CVE lane / IaC lane: no input.** `git diff --name-only 68658783..5a8810ac` over `pyproject.toml`, `poetry.lock`, `requirements*.txt`, `uv.lock`, `.github/**`, `Dockerfile*`, `docker-compose*`, `*.tf` returns empty — 0 new dependencies, 0 CVE findings by absence of a manifest, not by an unrun scan.

**Sweeps over the 150-file delta:** gitleaks-style scan (`AKIA|ASIA|-----BEGIN|password=|token=|api_key|secret_key|ghp_|github_pat_|xox[baprs]-|sk-…`) → the only matches are inside the prior verdict handoff's own description **of those patterns**. Zero home-absolute paths, IPs or e-mail literals in `specs/`, `tests/`, `dadaia_workspace/`, `hooks/` or `.github/`. The single UUID added to test fixtures is the synthetic `deadbeef-dead-4bee-8bee-deadbeefdead`, not a real session id. `dadaia public doctor` → `[ok] public-privacy`, `[ok] entities-derivation`, no `[drift]`.

**Positive:** FR5's `tests/helpers/scan_population.py::assert_populated` (wired into `tests/unit/features/panel/test_no_bearer_in_url.py` and siblings) stops a privacy/security scan test from passing vacuously on an empty file population — a direct hardening of the control class that failed silently twice before.

**Bug-surface axis (FR24).** `dadaia bugs stats`: 494 total, 475 resolved, 13 superseded, 1 open, 1 deferred, 4 rejected. The delta **reduces** the bug surface of the touched features: FR2 collapses 11 hand-kept atomic-write idioms into one `core` leaf (superseding `two-atomic-writers-leak-temp-file-on-injected-os-replace-failure`), FR6 replaces a twice-missed hand-kept field list with the schema-mirror tuple, FR1 removes a branch from the LAW predicate and derives `.dadaia` subdir truth from a single authority (closing `dadaia-reconcile-quarantines-sanctioned-references-clone`), and FR7 narrows an over-broad strip. Every one of those is a deletion or a collapse, not a puxadinho — the correct direction under the standing order. The HIGH finding above is a **content/privacy** defect in committed specs prose, not a structural regression.

decisions_required: Operator: scrub the foreign consumer repo slug from the 6 offending paths and rewrite the unpushed commits (36e074e7..HEAD) so all 13 objects are clean; re-run `dadaia ci push-gate-check` on the real refspec and require EXIT=0.
Operator: decide whether specs/releases/_ideas/0.5.0/** belongs on feature/0.4.5 at all — it carries 10 of the 13 offending objects and is out of the rc-1 scope.
